programmes.d: Oscar loses money in a poker game and when he can't pay the debt in cash, he donates Felix's band, the Sophisticados, to Billie Joe as payment instead.
When Oscar learns the park where he and his cronies played baseball is going to be the site for an office building, Oscar becomes civic-minded and decides to run for city councilman.

Singer-composer Paul Williams is the special guest star in this episode written especially for him. Felix Unger's daughter has a crush on Williams and runs away from home to follow him wherever he appears.
Felix discovers that his father and Oscar's knew each other in the old days and that Oscar's father was responsible for Felix's father's downfall.
Oscar Madison takes a job as a sports radio talk-show host but doesn't tell anyone until he finds out whether the station is going to make it permanent.
Oscar Madison falls in love with a beautiful woman who has two children he adores and before he knows it, he's engaged to be married and Felix prepares to lose a roommate.

Felix has a big commission riding on a new diet pill promotion but the model, "the fattest man in the world," suddenly decides he won't take the job. So Felix convinces Oscar Madison to put on a "fat suit" and pose in the "before" photograph.
When Oscar Madison finds a friend with inside information on his favorite sport, horse racing, he begins to win every bet.

Felix Unger is irate when given notice of another rent increase and organizes the entire building to go on strike until certain repairs and improvements are made to either justify the increase or cancel it altogether.
A pro hockey player hits Oscar and Felix, trying to patch things up, winds up challenging the athlete to a boxing match.
Felix and Oscar become roommates in the hospital in Hospital Mates.
Felix's pet parrot takes a turn for the worse, and Oscar, who never liked the bird, offers to handle the burial arrangements.
Over Oscar's objections, Felix recounts to their dates how they met while serving on a jury.

Felix volunteers on behalf of Oscar and himself to take care of a small boy. But on his first visit, the boy is indifferent to the cultural program Felix has planned and fascinated by sloppy Oscar and his hobbies and habits.

Felix takes refuge with friends Murray and Mimi when Oscar, in the throes of a hangover, asks him to leave in The Breakup. He is convinced that all he has to do is wait until Oscar feels better, but he is wrong.
Felix suspects Oscar when $50 is missing from the poker bank in The Blackout. Oscar tries to borrow money to get into the weekly poker game and learns his credit is even lower than his bankroll.
Felix is away on a photo assignment and Oscar is suspected of foul play.
Hogan takes Kinchloe to Paris to visit a friend of his who might help them get plans for the defense of Paris.
A disagreeable Russian pilot wants to escape,but refuses to go first to London. He wants to head east to Mother Russia.
Posing as waiters, the heroes want to get rid of a room full of German generals.
With Major Hochstetter in the camp, Hogan has extra trouble trying to smuggle out a bomber crew especially after they are moved from their usual barracks.
Planting a fuel depot right outside Stalag 13,a German general is tempting Hogan. Marya the White Russian also shows up again.
The location of a chemical plant is the prize when Hogan gets Carter to become a traitor.

Hooterville is abuzz as the townsfolk enter a contest sponsored by Peterson's Poi Juice, with a trip to Hawaii as the top prize. But no one expects the winner to be Arnold, the Ziffels' talented pig. Maybe a pig might fly after all, to the islands!

A charity rummage sale asks for donated clothing. Being among the wealthier residents of Hooterville, the organizers look to the Douglases. It isn't long before Oliver has to stop Lisa from giving away his entire wardrobe!

Love is in the air when Eb is quickly engaged to Loreli Appleby, whom he has only known for a day. Eb tries to impress Loreli's father, a farmer, but in typical fashion, he accidentally ruins his future father-in-law's cabbage crop.

When Fire Chief Joe Carson is looking for a way to go to Miami, he hires Oliver as his assistant, hoping Oliver will pay for the trip. The plan backfires, no pun intended, when Oliver starts pointing out what a poor job the chief has been doing.

The highways in Hooterville are in dire need of repair. Oliver is fed up and believes he can make a difference by complaining to his state representative, Ben Hanks. But Hanks' popularity proves greater than his sense of responsibility.

Lisa feels like she should be contributing more and wants to start working in Oliver's construction business. Lisa is like a fish out of water as she arrives to the Monroes' workshop in overalls and causes one problem after another.
Steve has a terrible day.
Robbie makes a deal to get a car and win the girl.
Mike announces that he has found his true love: Sally Ann Morrison.
Chip and his new pal Ernie go treasure hunting.

At the grocery store, Edith has an accident in the parking lot. She loses control of her shopping cart which smashes into a car and a can of Cling Peaches (in heavy syrup) flies out of the cart, onto the car, and makes a dent.

Mike is all stressed out with upcoming exams leaving him impotent and frustrated. Gloria encourages him to discuss it with her, but he refuses. Gloria confides in Edith what the problem is, and in turn she tells Archie.
After turning down the role of Scrooge in a Felix directed Christmas play, Oscar kicks Felix out of the apartment.
Felix persuades Oscar to use his influence to prevent a great college quarterback from being Corrupted by professional football.
Felix is forced to depend on Oscar's help in the finals of the Golden Apron cooking contest.
Felix and Oscar spend a rainy weekend in the country looking for a lost girl
Felix tries to make up with his divorced wife with a sentimental reminder of happier days.
Oscar develops a strong attachment for Felix's doctor, an attractive young woman.
Much to Oscar's disconfiture, Felix brings home an abandoned baby.
Felix and Oscar turn detectives to learn the source of the huge bankroll flaunted by the kid next door.
While his wife is away, Buddy moves in with the Petries and quickly wears out his welcome.
Rob's paternal pride suffers a cruel shock when he finds out that his six-year-old son is embarrassed to admit how his Dad makes a living.
Sally drags the entire gang to a bowling alley when she discovers a new dance sensation that's sure to sweep the nation.
Laura believes Rob, on jury duty, has been unfairly swayed by the beautiful blonde defendant.
